title: The glaze and the blue
description: Cards for borax, the glaze's flux, and cobalt oxide, the blue of Jaipur ware, each with its local name and what it does.

spec.heading: What the ware is made of

u0001.text: Jaipur ware is a body of ground quartz, painted with metal oxides and dipped in a glaze of glass, borax and lead oxide.

u0005.text: Borax powder is one of the glaze's ingredients, with crushed glass and red lead.

u0006.text: The glaze is made adhesive with boiled flour.

u0010.text: On firing, cobalt oxide becomes a deep blue.

u0011.text: The blue came from cobalt oxides first mined at Khetri.

C001.text: Blue pottery of Jaipur is based on ground quartz, and its GI application calls it primarily a ceramic body made of quartz.

quotes.quote: Blue Pottery is based on ground quartz.
Blue pottery of Jaipur and its surrounding villages is unique in that primarily it is a ceramic body made of quartz.

C014.text: The blue colour derives from jeypoorite and seypoorite, forms of cobalt oxide originally mined in the principality of Khetri in present-day Rajasthan.

quotes.quote: The distinct blue colour is derived from jeypoorite and seypoorite, forms of cobalt oxides that were originally mined in the principality of Khetri (in present-day Rajasthan).
Blue.-Obtained from cobalt from Khetri (Jaipur State).

C021.text: On firing, the oxide of cobalt becomes deep blue, chromium turns green, cadmium gives bright yellow and iron oxide becomes red-brown.

quotes.quote: The oxide of cobalt becomes a deep blue, that of chromium changes to green, cadmium produces a bright yellow and iron oxide becomes a red-brown.
iron may be used for red, cadmium for yellow and chromium for green

C030.text: After painting, the statement of case says, the piece is dipped into a homemade glaze of glass, borax and lead oxide made adhesive with boiled flour; it lists sindoor (red lead), suhaga (borax powder) and crushed glass.

quotes.quote: the unfired pieces are hand painted with oxide colours, dipped in clear glaze and fired once in wooden kilns.
The piece is then dipped into a homemade glaze of glass, borax and lead oxide which is made adhesive by the addition of boiled flour.
Glaze -,Sindoor (red lead), Suhaga (Borax powder), Crushed glass.
